text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT SEV2: automated alert - allocator page-bleed on gpu-node-12 (CUDA OOMs + container restarts). tagging eng-runtime and eng-oncall.

kai: seeing error spike ~10:12 UTC, gen requests 5xx. 3 containers restarted in 7m. metrics: token throughput down ~18%.

maria: confirmed, traces show paged-attention allocator memory growing slowly then sudden OOM at ~7.8GiB. likely fragmentation. logs attached below.

kai: paste of tail logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:11:58Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (12)
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] allocator: page_alloc: requested 4194304 bytes, free pages fragmented: 312
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] kvcache: resident_pages 124832 -> 141210
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] container: runtime restart triggered (OOM)
```

devon: repro steps? is this reproducing on a pinned node?

arjun: only on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-14 in the past hour. both are Ampere-80GB. suspect allocator fragmentation from paged-attn hot paths + long-lived KV entries.

maria: quick customer impact: ~2.7% of hosted generation requests are failing with 502/503. top affected tenants: team-alpha (3% of their calls), encoder-inc (1.2%). Not total outage but visible error rate spike.

kai: mitigation idea: rotate the warm pool off the two nodes, force cold start to different nodes, and trigger a controlled restart of the runtime to free fragmented pages. will that cause more customer impact?

arjun: controlled restart will drop active contexts for in-flight requests — small blips. We can schedule rolling restart per node with graceful drain on connections. fallback: route traffic to dedicated fallback model (smaller mem footprint) while we restart.

devon: steps I can take now: 1) drain gpu-node-12 from LB, 2) scale up warm pool by +2 in region-us-west, 3) restart inference runtime on node-12, then monitor.

maria: +1 to routing to smaller model as immediate fallback for high-priority tenants. adding canary route for team-alpha only first.

kai: executing drain now. command: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

arjun: while that's happening, capturing nvml stats:
```
nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(gpu0): total 85899345920, used 82345687040, free 3553658880
nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses: pid 12123 runtime-server (model X) 48000 MiB
```

oncall-bot: ALERT: drain started on gpu-node-12 by kai. Estimated 60s per pod graceful termination.

maria: I applied a temporary routing rule: high-err tenants -> model-small v2 (lower mem) with 30% traffic shift. Observing error rate dropping for team-alpha.

kai: restart done on node-12 runtime process `redwood-runtime` with SIGTERM -> restarted with fresh allocator. memory after restart: resident_pages down 40%.

sre-bot: NOTE: ephemeral kernel message seen during restart: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 4, GPU page table fault` — looks correlated with crash.

arjun: that Xid 4 means invalid page mapping/driver-level issue surfaced during heavy fragmentation. I'll open a follow-up with driver team if we see recurrence. For now, mitigation worked on node-12.

devon: node-14 still seeing creeping usage. I'll do the same rolling restart there after node-12 stabilizes.

maria: customer comms: ops-notify drafting short blurb to players affected; no SLA breach yet but heads-up.

kai: monitoring: post-restart 15m window shows healthy token throughput and error rate back to baseline for node-12. overall failure rate dropped from 2.7% -> 0.6%.

arjun: long-term: need allocator compaction and periodic slab defrag or background page-coalesce job to reclaim small fragments before they accumulate. adding an RFC ticket.

maria: action items:
- arjun: open driver/allocator ticket, include Xid logs and nvml dumps.
- devon: schedule rolling restart of gpu-node-14 in 20m with same drain plan.
- kai: add a temporary alert to detect sustained resident_pages growth (>5% over 10m) to catch slow creep earlier.
- maria: draft customer message and postmortem stub.

devon: ack, starting node-14 drain in 20m.

kai: one more note — enabled a short-lived cache eviction policy for KV entries older than 48h to reduce resident set growth; will monitor side-effects.

maria: if anyone sees weird regression after eviction toggle, ping infra immediately.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: node-12 stabilized, node-14 scheduled for rolling restart. severity remains SEV2 until node-14 completes and alerts quiet.

arjun: adding snippet for postmortem logs to attach:
```
# collect runtime allocator stats
curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep allocator_snapshot > /tmp/alloc-snap.txt
# nvml quick dump
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -x > /tmp/nvml-mem.xml
```

maria: will consolidate and create incident record in incidents/ with timeline and mitigation details.

kai: thanks all. handoff to night oncall in 2h — leaving runbook steps in thread.

devon: leaving after node-14 check. ping me if post-restart Xid repeats.

sre-bot: REMINDER: escalate to driver-team if Xid 4 appears >2x in 1h.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CLOSE PROVISIONAL: node-14 restart success, error rates normalized across region. marking as monitoring for 12h.

maria: provisional close noted. will file full postmortem once allocator ticket is created. :white_check_mark:
